candidates.name: scip-java
candidates.scope: Java symbol and reference indexing for supported build systems
candidates.evidence: Official documentation says indexing runs as part of the project build, automatic support is centered on Gradle and Maven, Java 17/21/25 need JVM exports, and indexing can clean compile caches and download dependencies.
candidates.measurements: Isolated v0.13.1, Maven 3.9.16, and Temurin 17 archives were checksum-verified; indexing did not start because JVM startup failed under the network-denied Seatbelt profile. See T2-scip-java-availability-2026-10-06.json.
candidates.reason: Build execution, cache side effects, dependency downloads, and build-system restrictions conflict with the default safe offline static scan. Adoption would require an explicit opt-in imported index workflow and identity validation, neither tested here.

candidates.name: scip-go
candidates.evidence: Official documentation installs the indexer with Go tooling and says it normally invokes Go commands for project information; alternative build-system support uses the Go Packages Driver protocol. Isolated D07 index evidence: T2-scip-go-availability-2026-10-06.json.
candidates.measurements: Isolated D07 index generated a SCIP artifact in 3.577 s with 108,609,536-byte maximum RSS; FlowWeave symbol/call comparison and human-labeled quality metrics were not run.

costs.packageSize: 19,021,394-byte scip-go binary; 68,100,347-byte Go toolchain archive; isolated workspace reached 587,150,836 bytes before cleanup.
costs.runtime: 39.184 s tool install and 3.577 s index run on one proposed D07 scope; exploratory only.
costs.rss: 108,609,536 bytes maximum resident set during the index run.
costs.offline: Not offline: go list fetched module dependencies through the isolated proxy; two requests reached proxy.golang.org.

candidates.reason: The D07 scope remains proposed. The probe proves index generation only; it does not compare source facts with FlowWeave or measure labeled quality. The indexer also required external Go modules, so the default offline scan and production adoption are not justified.

decision: Keep the current no-new-dependency analyzer pipeline. D01 shows dependency-cruiser's in-scope import pairs are a subset of FlowWeave's unlabeled output; Graphology has only synthetic algorithm smoke evidence; SCIP-Go generated one exploratory D07 index but was not compared to labeled facts; SCIP-Java indexing did not start. No candidate has human-labeled quality evidence sufficient for production adoption.
openRequirements: Use independently reviewed labels to assess accuracy and call coverage; D01 currently provides only hash-bound, unlabeled structural overlap (315 shared import pairs and 212 additional FlowWeave pairs), not precision, recall, or relative quality.
